profile.reading:
VIRTBIZ is a family-owned internet hosting and colocation company based at 2805 Canton Street in the Deep Ellum Public Improvement District, just east of downtown Dallas, Texas. The company describes itself as a 30-year veteran of the Dallas hosting market, and according to its own published materials it owns the building that houses its data center outright rather than leasing space in a third-party facility, giving it direct control over the property and its infrastructure rather than operating through a landlord or wholesale colocation provider.

Deep Ellum is one of Dallas's oldest neighborhoods, a former warehouse and entertainment district that has become a mixed-use area of music venues, restaurants, and small and mid-sized businesses just outside the central business district. A locally owned data center in that setting serves a different niche than the hyperscale campuses built by cloud providers and large wholesale operators in outlying parts of the metro area. VIRTBIZ markets itself to small and mid-sized businesses, web developers, and agencies needing shared web hosting, virtual private servers marketed as Elastic Cloud, dedicated servers under the name Metal Cloud, and traditional colocation space on a raised floor, along with SSL certificates and domain registration services bundled in.

The company holds preferred partner status with cPanel, the widely used web hosting control panel, and hosts infrastructure for BlueOnyx, an open-source server management platform, positioning itself within the control-panel-based shared and dedicated hosting market rather than the enterprise or hyperscale segment. VIRTBIZ advertises direct, in-house technical staffing, describing its support as fully staffed with dedicated technicians based in the United States, and highlights emergency migration services for customers moving away from other providers on short notice.

VIRTBIZ does not publish a specific power capacity, total square footage, or third-party certification such as a Tier rating or SOC audit for its Dallas facility, which is typical of small, independently owned hosting operators whose customers are generally more interested in service responsiveness and price than in formal data center certifications. The absence of those published figures reflects the company's scale and market segment rather than any unusual gap in disclosure, and its facility is best understood as a boutique, owner-operated hosting environment serving a regional small business customer base rather than a large-scale wholesale or hyperscale data center.

reading.body:
VIRTBIZ operates a data center in Dallas under its own ownership and management, with a 30-year history in the Texas hosting market. The facility's power capacity and physical specifications are not published on the operator's homepage, which prevents any estimate of its role in AI infrastructure scaling.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 18 publish power capacity figures totaling 468 megawatts. VIRTBIZ does not appear in the published capacity rankings because no megawatt specification is available from its operator.

Without disclosed power specifications, this facility cannot be assessed for its materiality to AI deployment or its contribution to the state's compute infrastructure. The operator's long tenure in the Dallas market suggests operational experience, but no public data connects this to current or planned AI workloads.
